statements.claim: The treasury of Indraprastha had grown so heavy that no one imagined it could be emptied in a hundred years.
statements.evidence: MB 2.32: 'The large treasure room of the king became so much filled with hoards of wealth virtuously obtained that it could not be emptied even in a hundred years.'

statements.claim: In those days of Yudhishthira's rule, clouds poured exactly as much rain as the people wished, fields and herds and trade flourished, and the kingdom knew no drought, flood, plague, or fire.
statements.evidence: MB 2.32: 'clouds in his kingdom poured as much rain as the people desired, and the cities and the town became highly prosperous... cattle bleeding, agriculture and trade prospered highly... There were no droughts and floods and plagues and fires and premature deaths.'

statements.claim: Even thieves and cheats gave up lying when they dealt with each other, and foreign kings came to the court only to serve, to worship, or to offer tribute that would not impoverish them — never to fight.
statements.evidence: MB 2.32: 'even robbers and cheats never spoke lies amongst themselves... It was only for doing agreeable services, or for worshipping, or for offering tributes that would not impoverish, that other kings used to approach Yudhisthira (and not for hostility or battle).'

statements.claim: Yudhishthira's friends and ministers approached, each separately and all together, urging the sacrifice without delay, and Yudhishthira, weighing his treasury, fixed his heart on the Rajasuya.
statements.evidence: MB 2.32: 'His friends and officers, each separately and all together, approaching him said,--"The time hath come, O exalted one, for thy sacrifice. Let arrangements... be made without loss of time."' and 'the son of Kunti... fixed his heart upon the celebration of a sacrifice.'

statements.claim: The Rajasuya was a sacrifice that belonged to emperors, said to purify everything it touched.
statements.evidence: BP 10.72.1-10 excerpt: Yudhishthira 'wishes to perform the purifying Rajasuya sacrifice'; MB 2.32: Krishna says 'Thou... deservest imperial dignity. Let, therefore, the great sacrifice be performed by thee.'

statements.claim: Krishna came to Indraprastha at the head of a great host, chariot wheels rattling, bringing a large mass of treasure — an inexhaustible ocean of gems — and leaving the Yadava army in Vasudeva's command.
statements.evidence: MB 2.32: 'having appointed Vasudeva to the command of the (Yadava) army, and bringing with him for the king Yudhishthira just a large mass of treasure... himself surrounded by a mighty host and filling the atmosphere with the rattle of his chariot-wheels... that inexhaustible ocean of gems he had brought.'

statements.claim: The capital was gladdened by his presence the way a dark region is gladdened by the sun, or still air by a gentle breeze.
statements.evidence: MB 2.32: 'The capital of the Bharata was gladdened by Krishna's presence just as a dark region is rendered joyful by the sun or a region of still air by a gentle breeze.'

statements.claim: Yudhishthira stood before the seated Krishna with Dhaumya, Dwaipayana and the other sacrificial priests, and with Bhima, Arjuna and the twins.
statements.evidence: MB 2.32: 'the son of Pandu, with Dhaumya and Dwaipayana and the other sacrificial priests and with Bhima and Arjuna and the twins, addressed Krishna.'

statements.claim: Yudhishthira told Krishna the whole earth was under his sway for Krishna's sake, that his wealth came through Krishna's grace, and asked permission to celebrate the sacrifice with his brothers, inviting Krishna to install himself at the rite or to permit Yudhishthira's own installation.
statements.evidence: MB 2.32: 'O Krishna it is for thee that the whole earth is under my sway... it is through thy grace that vast wealth had been got by me... I desire to devote that wealth according to the ordinance, unto superior Brahmanas and the carrier of sacrificial libations... grant me permission to celebrate a sacrifice... install thyself at that sacrifice... Or... permit me to be installed at the sacrifice along with these my younger brothers.'

statements.claim: Krishna answered that Yudhishthira deserved imperial dignity, that after conquering all the kings and gathering the requisites the sacrifice should be performed and none could surpass him in splendor, not even the gods, and asked to be employed in some office, saying he would obey all commands.
statements.evidence: MB 2.32: 'Thou... deservest imperial dignity. Let... the great sacrifice be performed by thee... Employ me also in some office... I should obey all thy commands.' BP 10.72.1-10 excerpt: 'after conquering all the kings and gathering the requisites the sacrifice should be performed, and... none can surpass Yudhishthira in splendor, not even the gods.'

statements.claim: Yudhishthira replied that his resolve was already crowned with fruit since Krishna had arrived agreeably to his wish.
statements.evidence: MB 2.32: 'Yudhisthira replied--O Krishna, my resolve is already crowned with fruit, and success also is surely mine, when thou, O Harishikesa, hast arrived here agreeably to my wish!'

statements.claim: Commanded by Krishna, Yudhishthira and his brothers collected the materials for the Rajasuya, and the first order went to Sahadeva and all his ministers to appoint persons to gather the needed articles.
statements.evidence: MB 2.32: 'Commanded by Krishna, the son of Pandu along with his brothers set himself upon collecting the materials for the performance of the Rajasuya sacrifice... commanded Sahadeva... and all ministers also, saying,--Let persons be appointed to collect without loss of time, all those article[s].'

statements.claim: "Yet no one thought of that wealth as greed made visible" and the closing image of the brothers measuring what the world owed them.
statements.evidence: Moralizing/atmospheric framing of the kingdom's prosperity and the turn toward conquest; no specific source claim.

notes: Blends MB 2.32 (prosperity, arrival, dialogue) with BP 10.72 (purifying Rajasuya, 'none can surpass even the gods'); both are cited in the pack. No UNSUPPORTED or CONTRADICTED claims.

statements.claim: Yudhishthira sent Sahadeva to the south, Nakula to the west, Arjuna to the north, and Bhima to the east.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (BP 10.72.11-13): 'Sahadeva to the south, Nakula to the west, Arjuna to the north, and Bhima to the east'; Sanskrit v.12: 'sahadevaṃ dakṣiṇasyām ādiśat' (Sahadeva dispatched southwards).

statements.claim: Sahadeva, the youngest, was sent with the Srijnayas, his allied warriors.
statements.evidence: BP 10.72.12: 'sahadevaṃ dakṣiṇasyām ādiśat saha sṛñjayaiḥ' (dispatched Sahadeva southwards together with the Srijnayas); Sahadeva being the youngest Pandava is standard within the corpus.

statements.claim: The brothers vanquished the kings of the four quarters and carried back abundant wealth for the sacrifice.
statements.evidence: BP 10.72.13: 'te vijitya nṛpān vīrā ājahrur digbhya ojasā' (those heroes, having conquered the kings, brought wealth from the directions); pack excerpt: 'They vanquish the kings and bring back abundant wealth for the sacrifice.'

statements.claim: From every direction the tribute moved toward Indraprastha, and the returning brothers' wealth poured into the treasury.
statements.evidence: Pack summary: 'they return laden with tribute for the sacrifice'; index excerpt: 'they return laden with tribute.'

statements.claim: Directional color — southern kings' 'ancient thrones,' western 'sea kingdoms and the sunset,' northern 'mountain kings' in their passes, eastern quarter 'of the rising sun' — and the homecoming descriptions (wagons heavy, wealth of sea/mountain lords).
statements.evidence: Atmospheric elaboration consistent with each brother's assigned quarter; the pack gives no per-direction campaign detail.

statements.claim: The priests rehearsed rites, craftsmen raised halls, and Indraprastha waited and questioned travelers for news while the brothers were away.
statements.evidence: Generic connective scene-setting for the interval of the campaigns; not contradicted by the pack.

notes: Evidence pack is thin (only vv.12-13 in Sanskrit); the individual direction assignments for Nakula/Arjuna/Bhima rest on the pack's own excerpt and index summary, which the story follows exactly. No UNSUPPORTED or CONTRADICTED.

statements.claim: Shishupala, son of Damaghosha, king of Chedi, rose from his seat, raised his arm, and spoke harsh, fearless words, enraged by hearing Krishna's praises.
statements.evidence: BP 10.74.29: 'damaghoṣa-sutaḥ sva-pīṭhād utthāya kṛṣṇa-guṇa-varṇana-jāta-manyuḥ... utkṣipya bāhum... paruṣāṇy abhītaḥ' (son of Damaghosha rose from his seat, anger born of hearing Krishna's virtues described, raised his arm, spoke harsh words fearlessly).

statements.claim: Shishupala mocked the assembly for honoring a cowherd before men of austerity and learning whose sins were burned away by knowledge.
statements.evidence: BP 10.74.31-33: 'yūyaṃ pātra-vidāṃ śreṣṭhā mā mandhvaṃ bāla-bhāṣītam / tapo-vidyā-vrata-dharān jñāna-vidhvasta-kalmaṣān... gopālaḥ kula-pāṃsanaḥ' (do not take this for a child's babble... passing over the austerity/knowledge-bearing, sin-washed lords of the assembly, a cowherd, defiler of his family).

statements.claim: He accused Krishna of abandoning his order — cast out of every duty of caste and stage of life, stripped of all dharma — and spoke of the line of Yayati being cursed and driven out and of lost priestly splendor.
statements.evidence: BP 10.74.34-36: 'varṇāśrama-kulāpetaḥ sarva-dharma-bahiṣ-kṛtaḥ / yayātinaiṣāṃ hi kulaṃ śaptaṃ sadbhir bahiṣ-kṛtam / brahmarṣi-sevitān deśān hitvaite 'brahma-varcasam.'

statements.claim: Shishupala mocked Krishna's deeds — slaying a vulture in infancy was nothing remarkable, and holding up Govardhan for a week was like an anthill to a strong man.
statements.evidence: MB 2.41: 'If Krishna in his infancy slew a vulture, what is there remarkable in that... what is there remarkable in this one's having supported for a week the Govardhan mount which is like an anthill?'

statements.claim: He spoke of Jarasandha, the great king slain in his own city, calling the slayer a wretch of the Vrishni race who killed him unrighteously.
statements.evidence: MB 2.37: 'This wretch born in the race of the Vrishnis unrighteously slew of old the illustrious king Jarasandha.'

statements.claim: The sages in the hall stopped their ears at the blasphemy and cursed him; the angry Pandavas — Bhima blazing — rose with their allies the Matsyas, Kaikayas and Srijnayas to slay him.
statements.evidence: BP 10.74.38-40 (assembly hears the unbearable censure; 'tataḥ pāṇḍu-sutāḥ kruddhā matsya-kaikaya-sṛñjayāḥ'); pack index: 'The assembled sages stop their ears and curse him, and the enraged Pandavas and their allies rise with weapons to slay him'; MB 2.41: 'Bhimasena endued with energy became angry.'

statements.claim: Yudhishthira pleaded with Shishupala that his words were scarcely proper, sinful and needlessly cruel, that he should not insult Bhishma, and that the older kings approved the worship of Krishna, whom Bhishma knows truly.
statements.evidence: MB 2.37, Yudhishthira's speech nearly verbatim: 'what thou hast said is scarcely proper for thee... highly sinful and needlessly cruel. Insult not Bhishma... these many kings, older than thou art, all approve of the worship offered unto Krishna... Bhishma knoweth Krishna truly. Thou knowest him not so well.'

statements.claim: Bhishma said that he who disapproves the worship of Krishna, the oldest one in the universe, deserves neither soft words nor conciliation; that every king in the assembly had been vanquished by Krishna's energy; that Krishna deserves worship by the three worlds; that the first worship was offered for his fame, heroism and success; and that Shishupala is a mere boy who does not know Krishna.
statements.evidence: MB 2.37, Bhishma's speech nearly verbatim: 'He that approveth not the worship offered unto Krishna, the oldest one in the universe, deserveth neither soft words nor conciliation... I do not behold in this assembly of kings even one ruler of men who hath not been vanquished in battle by the energy of this son of the Satwata race... he deserveth to be worshipped by the three worlds also... We have offered unto him the first worship because of his fame, his heroism, his success... This Sisupala is a mere boy and hence he knoweth not Krishna.'

statements.claim: The mighty-armed Bhishma caught hold of Shishupala, as Mahadeva seizes his own son.
statements.evidence: MB 2.41: 'the mighty-armed Bhishma caught him like Mahadeva seizing Mahasena.'

statements.claim: The king of Chedi stood unperturbed, seized sword and shield, and stood ready in the middle of the hall.
statements.evidence: BP 10.74.41: 'tataś caidyas tv asambhrānto jagṛhe khaḍga-carmaṇī' (then the Chedi king, unperturbed, seized sword and shield).

statements.claim: 'His face black with fury' and the closing metaphor of a storm gathered over one figure.
statements.evidence: Visual/atmospheric embellishment of the rage attested in BP 10.74.29; no specific sourceable fact.

notes: Blends BP 10.74.29-41 (outburst, assembly reaction, sword-and-shield) with MB 2.37 (conciliation speeches) and MB 2.41 (mockery, Bhishma's seizure) — all listed as this story's sources. Follows the BP variant (Shishupala stays and seizes weapons) rather than MB 2.37's departure line; consistent with the pack's canonical event and the next story (Krishna Slays Shishupala). No UNSUPPORTED or CONTRADICTED.

statements.claim: It was Krishna — the lord of the lords of yoga, as the chronicle names him — who completed the great Rajasuya rite for the king.
statements.evidence: BP 10.74.47: 'sādhayitvā kratu rājñaḥ kṛṣṇo yogeśvareśvaraḥ' (Krishna, lord of the lords of yoga, having accomplished the sacrifice for the king).

statements.claim: Krishna bestowed ample gifts without stint on the officiating priests and all who had sat in the assembly; no one who served the rite went away empty-handed.
statements.evidence: BP 10.74.46: 'ṛtvigbhyaḥ sa-sadasyebhyo dakṣiṇāṃ vipulām adāt' (he gave ample dakshina to the priests together with the assembly members).

statements.claim: The avabhritha, the concluding bath, followed, and Yudhishthira bathed and was cleansed.
statements.evidence: BP 10.74.50: 'rājasūyāvabhṛthyena snāto rājā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ' (king Yudhishthira bathed with the Rajasuya's avabhritha).

statements.claim: Krishna stayed on in Indraprastha month after month and, when he asked leave, Yudhishthira was reluctant to give it; Krishna departed toward his own city (Dwaraka).
statements.evidence: BP 10.74.48: 'tato 'nujñāpya rājānam anicchantam apīśvaraḥ' (then, taking leave of the unwilling king, the Lord departed); pack excerpt: 'after some months takes leave of the reluctant Yudhishthira and returns to his own city.'

statements.claim: Gods, men and the beings of the air, every one of them honored by the king as they departed, carried away praise of Krishna and of the sacrifice.
statements.evidence: BP 10.74.51: 'rājñā sabhājitāḥ sarve sura-mānava-khecarāḥ' (all gods, men and sky-goers were honored by the king); pack excerpt: 'All the assembled guests depart praising Krishna and the sacrifice.'

statements.claim: One guest alone differed: Duryodhana — the wicked one, the strife itself, the disease of the Kuru line — could not endure the Pandavas' prosperity and carried his grievance toward Hastinapura.
statements.evidence: BP 10.74.52: 'duryodhanam ṛte pāpaṃ kaliṃ kuru-kulāmayam' (except wicked Duryodhana, the Kali [strife], the disease of the Kuru race); pack excerpt: 'except the wicked Duryodhana, who could not endure the Pandavas' prosperity'; return to Hastinapura/Gajahvaya consistent with BP 10.75.38 ('prayayau gajāhvayam').

statements.claim: Closing speculation that Duryodhana 'would spend the coming months trying to undo' the Pandavas' greatness, and that his grievance 'arrived before any of the praise did.'
statements.evidence: Foreshadowing/atmosphere consistent with the envy the pack attests; not a specific sourceable fact in 10.74.46-52.

notes: All key claims map 1:1 onto BP 10.74.46-52 and the pack excerpt. The 'fires... allowed to grow quiet' and emperor-crowning imagery are atmospheric connective narration. No UNSUPPORTED or CONTRADICTED.

statements.claim: The assembly hall in which Duryodhana was deceived was built by Maya, the great architect, for Yudhishthira.
statements.evidence: BP 10.75.33: 'sabhāyāṃ maya-kḷptāyāṃ' (in the hall fashioned by Maya).

statements.claim: Duryodhana came to Yudhishthira's sacrifice with his brothers and burned with envy at the splendor of the palace.
statements.evidence: BP 10.75.30-31: 'vīkṣya duryodhanaḥ śriyam... viṣakta-hṛdayaḥ kuru-rāḍ atapyat' (Duryodhana, seeing the splendor, the Kuru king burned, his heart poisoned); 10.75.35: 'tatra duryodhano mānī parīto bhrātṛbhir' (proud Duryodhana, surrounded by his brothers); presence at the Rajasuya established by DKS_0399 (BP 10.74.52) and the corpus chain.

statements.claim: The hall's splendor seemed gathered from the wealth of earthly kings, lords of demons, and Indra himself.
statements.evidence: BP 10.75.31: 'yasmiṃs narendra-ditijendra-surendra-lakṣmīr nānā vibhānti' (in which the glories of earthly kings, lord of the demons and lord of the gods shone variously).

statements.claim: Duryodhana, seeing crystal floor as water, gathered his garment to keep it dry and stepped forward onto hard, dry crystal.
statements.evidence: BP 10.75.36: 'sthale 'bhyagṛhṇād vastrāntaṃ jalaṃ matvā' (on dry ground he lifted the hem of his garment, taking it for water); pack excerpt: 'mistakes a crystal floor for water and lifts his garment.'

statements.claim: Then, before a real pool so clear it seemed to continue as floor, Duryodhana walked into the water and fell.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'then falls where he thought the floor was, deceived by the illusion'; index summary: 'mistakes water for floor and falls.'

statements.claim: Bhima laughed first and loudest, and the women of the court and the other kings laughed with him, though Yudhishthira made a sign for restraint.
statements.evidence: BP 10.75.37: 'jahāsa bhīmas taṃ dṛṣṭvā striyo nṛpatayo pare' (Bhima laughed seeing him; the women and the other kings too); pack excerpt: 'Bhima and the women laugh despite the king's restraint.'

statements.claim: Duryodhana, ashamed and blazing with rage, departed in silence and returned to Hastinapura.
statements.evidence: BP 10.75.38: 'sa vrīḍito 'vag-vadano ruṣā jvalan niṣkramya tūṣṇīṃ prayayau gajāhvayam' (he, ashamed, face downcast, blazing with rage, went out silently and departed to Gajahvaya [Hastinapura]).

statements.claim: Krishna watched in silence, intent on relieving the burden the earth carried, and let Duryodhana carry the humiliation home.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'while Krishna remains silent, intent on relieving the earth's burden'; Krishna is listed among the story's characters in the pack index.

statements.claim: 'Duryodhana, king of Hastinapura' — royal title applied to Duryodhana.
statements.evidence: The pack's own Sanskrit verses style him as ruler: BP 10.75.31 'kuru-rāḍ' and 10.75.35 'nṛpa'; the phrase is consistent with source usage.

statements.claim: Servants hiding smiles, the hall as 'a second heaven,' and the closing reflections on the slow work of the kings' pride.
statements.evidence: Atmospheric connective narration around the attested deception and laughter; no specific source claim.

notes: The two-step illusion (crystal-as-water, then water-as-floor) follows the pack excerpt/index reading of BP 10.75.36 and the classic account. No UNSUPPORTED or CONTRADICTED.

statements.claim: Shalva was the friend of Shishupala, whom Krishna had struck down at the Rajasuya sacrifice.
statements.evidence: BP 10.76.1: 'śiśupāla-sakhaḥ śālvo' (Shalva, friend of Shishupala); Shishupala's slaying at the Rajasuya is the prior corpus event (DKS_0398, BP 10.74.42-46) referenced by the pack's chain.

statements.claim: Shalva had been at Rukmini's wedding in the company that came to claim her and went away defeated; the Yadavas had humbled him once and now killed his friend.
statements.evidence: BP 10.76.1: 'rukmiṇy-udvāha āgataḥ' (he had come to Rukmini's wedding); pack excerpt: 'who had been defeated at Rukmini's wedding.'

statements.claim: In the hearing of all the kings Shalva vowed to make the earth empty of Yadavas.
statements.evidence: BP 10.76.2: 'śālvaḥ pratijñām akaroc chṛṇvatāṃ sarva-bhūbhujām' (Shalva made a vow in the hearing of all kings); pack excerpt: 'vows before the kings to make the earth devoid of Yadavas.'

statements.claim: Shalva went to the Himalayas and worshipped Shiva, the Pasupati, husband of Uma, eating nothing but a handful of dust each day for a year.
statements.evidence: BP 10.76.3-4: 'devaṃ paśu-patiṃ prabhum... saṃvatsarānte bhagavān āśu-toṣa umā-patiḥ' (he [worshipped] the lord Pasupati; at year's end the quickly-contented Lord, husband of Uma); pack excerpt: 'eating a handful of dust each day, and after a year Shiva, easily pleased, offers him a boon'; Himalayas given as the location in the pack's index entry.

statements.claim: Shalva asked for a citadel that no god, demon, man, gandharva, serpent, or rakshasa could overcome — a city moving through the sky at its master's will.
statements.evidence: BP 10.76.5: 'devāsura-manuṣyāṇāṃ gandharvoraga-rakṣasām' (of gods, demons, men, gandharvas, serpents, rakshasas — the list of powers named in the boon); BP 10.76.7: 'sa labdhvā kāma-gaṃ yānaṃ' (he obtained the will-moving vehicle).

statements.claim: Shiva consented and gave the making of the city to Maya, the architect called the conqueror of enemy cities, who built Saubha — dark, hard to assail, moving at its master's will.
statements.evidence: BP 10.76.6-7: 'tatheti giriśādiṣṭo mayaḥ para-puraṃ-jayaḥ / sa labdhvā kāma-gaṃ yānaṃ tamo-dhāma durāsadam' ('so be it'; commanded by the mountain-lord, Maya the conqueror of enemy cities; he obtained the will-moving vehicle, the abode of darkness, difficult to assail).

statements.claim: The wise named it the abode of darkness, for it sailed wrapped in a gloom of its own.
statements.evidence: BP 10.76.7: 'tamo-dhāma' (abode of darkness) is the source's own epithet for Saubha.

statements.claim: Shalva's purpose in obtaining Saubha was vengeance against Dwaraka and the house of the Yadavas.
statements.evidence: Vow to empty the earth of Yadavas (BP 10.76.2) plus the siege of Krishna's city that immediately follows in BP 10.76.8-11 and DKS_0402; Dwaraka listed as target in the pack index.

statements.claim: Growth thin as a shadow through a year of snows, and the 'easily pleased' gloss on Shiva.
statements.evidence: Atmospheric elaboration of the year-long austerity (BP 10.76.3-4); 'āśu-toṣa' (swiftly contented) supports the character gloss.

notes: The 'iron' quality of Saubha is carried over from the corpus chain titles ('flying iron city'); nothing in the pack contradicts it (BP here stresses tamo-dhāma and durāsadam). No UNSUPPORTED or CONTRADICTED.

statements.claim: Shalva came to Dwaraka in the self-moving, impenetrable flying city Saubha with a vast army and besieged the city.
statements.evidence: BP 10.76.7-8: 'sa labdhvā kāma-gaṃ yānaṃ tamo-dhāma durāsadam / nirudhya senayā śālvo mahatyā' (having obtained the will-moving vehicle, the hard-to-assail abode of darkness, Shalva besieged with a great army); pack excerpt: 'Shalva flies to Dwaraka... and with a vast army.'

statements.claim: Shalva remembered the enmity of the Vrishnis — his friend Shishupala dead at the Rajasuya and his own defeat at Rukmini's wedding.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'Shalva flies to Dwaraka remembering the enmity of the Vrishnis'; the specific grievances are established in DKS_0401's pack (BP 10.76.1-2).

statements.claim: From Saubha there rained weapons, stones, whole trees torn up by the roots, thunderbolts that split the towers, serpents, and showers of gravel.
statements.evidence: BP 10.76.10: 'śilā-drumāś cāśanayaḥ sarpā āsāra-śarkarāḥ' (stones, trees, thunderbolts, serpents, showers of gravel).

statements.claim: The gardens and famous groves were shredded; gates, walls, palaces, ramparts and upper terraces were shattered, dented and cracked.
statements.evidence: BP 10.76.9: 'sa-gopurāṇi dvārāṇi prāsādāṭṭāla-tolikāḥ' (the gates with their towers, palaces, ramparts, upper terraces); pack excerpt: 'shatters its gardens and gates'; BP 10.76.11: 'ity ardyamānā saubhena kṛṣṇasya nagarī bhṛśam' (thus Krishna's city was severely afflicted by Saubha).

statements.claim: Pradyumna, Krishna's son by Rukmini, seeing his people afflicted, mounted his chariot and cried 'Do not fear,' rallying the city.
statements.evidence: BP 10.76.12: 'pradyumno bhagavān vīkṣya bādhyamānā nijāḥ prajāḥ' (the blessed Pradyumna, seeing his own people afflicted); pack excerpt: 'mounts his chariot and cries "Do not fear"'; Rukmini's son per BP 10.76.16 ('rukmiṇī-sutaḥ').

statements.claim: Satyaki, Charudeshna, Samba, and Akrura with his younger brothers sallied forth, followed by the great archers and leaders of the chariot troops.
statements.evidence: BP 10.76.13-14: 'sātyakiś cārudeṣṇaś ca sāmbo 'krūraḥ sahānujaḥ / apare ca maheṣv-āsā ratha-yūthapa-yūthapāḥ.'

statements.claim: A battle raged between Shalva's host and the Yadavas; Pradyumna countered the illusions of the lord of Saubha with divine weapons.
statements.evidence: BP 10.76.15-16: 'tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ śālvānāṃ yadubhiḥ saha / tāś ca saubha-pater māyā divyāstrai rukmiṇī-sutaḥ.'

statements.claim: Krishna was not among the defenders: he had gone to Indraprastha, summoned by Yudhishthira for the sacrifice, and no news of the siege had reached him.
statements.evidence: BP 10.77.5: 'indraprasthaṃ gataḥ kṛṣṇa āhūto dharma-sūnunā' (Krishna had gone to Indraprastha, summoned by Dharma's son — cited in DKS_0403's pack and the corpus chain); DKS_0403's pack excerpt confirms he learned of the attack only by omens, i.e. not by news.

statements.claim: Terror as Shalva's real weapon — a siege from the sky that could not be answered — and the description of the city as 'golden... by the sea.'
statements.evidence: Interpretive framing of the terror the pack's summary attests ('terrifying its people'); Dwaraka's seaside setting is standard within the corpus.

notes: Krishna's absence is grounded in the immediate successor passage (BP 10.77.5, in DKS_0403's pack) and the pack's variant note, since DKS_0402's own excerpt narrates only the siege. No UNSUPPORTED or CONTRADICTED.

statements.claim: Krishna had gone to Indraprastha, summoned by Yudhishthira for the Rajasuya.
statements.evidence: BP 10.77.5: 'indraprasthaṃ gataḥ kṛṣṇa āhūto dharma-sūnunā' (Krishna had gone to Indraprastha, summoned by Dharma's son); pack excerpt: 'Krishna, summoned to Indraprastha for the Rajasuya.'

statements.claim: Krishna took leave of the elders of the Kurus, the sages, and Pritha his aunt with her sons.
statements.evidence: BP 10.77.6: 'kuru-vṛddhān anujñāpya munīṃś ca sa-sutāṃ pṛthām' (taking leave of the Kuru elders, the sages, and Pritha with her sons); Pritha (Kunti) is Krishna's aunt, and the Pandavas are 'her sons.'

statements.claim: Krishna perceived dire omens that his own people were in danger and hurried back to Dwaraka.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'returns to Dwaraka perceiving dire omens'; BP 10.77.8: 'vīkṣya tat kadanaṃ svānāṃ' (seeing the slaughter of his own people).

statements.claim: On arrival Krishna saw the ruin of his own people and understood that the allies of the Chaidya — the friends of the slain Shishupala — had attacked his city while he was away.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'realizing the Chaidya's allies have attacked his city'; BP 10.77.8: 'vīkṣya tat kadanaṃ svānāṃ nirūpya pura-rakṣaṇam.'

statements.claim: Krishna ordered Daruka, his charioteer: 'Bring my chariot. Quickly. Straight to Shalva,' and Daruka drove the chariot out against Shalva.
statements.evidence: BP 10.77.9-10: 'rathaṃ prāpaya me sūta śālvasyāntikam āśu vai... ity uktaś codayām āsa ratham āsthāya dārukaḥ' (Bring my chariot, O charioteer, quickly to Shalva; thus addressed, Daruka mounted and drove the chariot).

statements.claim: Shalva's army was already nearly broken by the Yadava princes when Krishna arrived.
statements.evidence: BP 10.77.11: 'hata-prāya-baleśvaraḥ' (whose forces were nearly destroyed).

statements.claim: Shalva hurled a blazing spear at Daruka, the charioteer, which came down like a great meteor.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'hurls a blazing spear at Krishna's charioteer'; BP 10.77.12: 'tām āpatantīṃ nabhasi maholkām iva raṃhasā' (it fell from the sky with the speed of a great meteor).

statements.claim: Krishna's arrows met the spear in mid-air and cut it into a hundred pieces.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'which Krishna cuts to a hundred pieces with his arrows.'

statements.claim: Krishna pierced Shalva with sixteen shafts, and the flying city Saubha reeled through the sky.
statements.evidence: BP 10.77.13: 'taṃ ca ṣoḍaśabhir viddhvā bānaiḥ saubhaṃ ca khe bhramat' (piercing him with sixteen arrows, and Saubha wandered in the sky).

statements.claim: Shalva's arrow struck Krishna's left arm — the arm holding Sharnga — and a great cry of lamentation went up from the beings watching.
statements.evidence: BP 10.77.14-15: 'śālvaḥ śaures tu doḥ savyaṃ sa-śārṅgaṃ śārṅga-dhanvanaḥ / hāhā-kāro mahān āsīd bhūtānāṃ tatra paśyatām' (Shalva [struck] the left arm of Shauri together with Sharnga, of the bearer of the Sharnga bow; a great cry of lamentation arose from the beings watching there).

statements.claim: His people fought on without him while he was away, and the siege continued until Krishna's return.
statements.evidence: BP 10.76.15 (battle of Shalva's host with the Yadus) narrated before Krishna's arrival in BP 10.77; consistent with DKS_0402.

statements.claim: The claim that the battle 'rose into the sky' and that Krishna 'brought the war its answer' by pressing on.
statements.evidence: Forward-looking connective narration consistent with Saubha reeling in the sky (BP 10.77.13) and the continuation of the duel in subsequent verses; not a specific sourceable assertion within 10.77.5-18.

statements.claim: 'In the middle of the honors and ceremonies of the Rajasuya' as the timing of Krishna's departure.
statements.evidence: BP 10.77.5-6 places the summons at the Rajasuya visit; DKS_0399's pack had Krishna lingering in Indraprastha after the rite, so the exact phase of the ceremony is a connective gloss — the siege-during-the-Rajasuya-visit frame is what 10.77.5 supports.

notes: Cross-story note: DKS_0399's pack (BP 10.74.48) has Krishna leave Indraprastha after the completed Rajasuya, while DKS_0402/0403 (BP 10.77.5) have the siege occur during his Rajasuya summons — a telescoping present in the source itself; each story is faithful to its own pack. No UNSUPPORTED or CONTRADICTED.
